deathSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Heidi Diallo. Carpenter. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Trail compass, Carpenter's square, Dead Phone, Contract Quill, Boot stone. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. You heard it in the dark. Breathing. Not yours. It knew your name — it said it wrong, like it learned the shape of the sound but not what it meant.

🔥 The fire settles. Moisés has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Nevermore — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Desmond mutters "We've been walking past those." Carmela asks "Say that again — slower." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
